lessons.title: Découverte des lignes
lessons.oneGoal: Students recognize that lines are everywhere in their environment

visualSupports: Tape lines on floor as examples

then.plan: Use student bodies as lines - lie down straight for 'droit', curl up for 'courbe'. Dance with line movements to music.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Lines in classroom objects, clothing patterns, and body movements

lessons.title: Lignes avec le corps
lessons.oneGoal: Students create different types of lines using their bodies and gestures

then.plan: Teacher provides rhythm with clapping or simple songs. Students can create their own rhythm sounds for line movements.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Body movements create invisible lines in dance and sports

lessons.title: Lignes émotionnelles
lessons.oneGoal: Students understand that different line qualities express different feelings

then.plan: Use colored pencils or crayons. Focus more on body movement emotions and tracing emotions in sand trays or on rough paper.

lessons.realWorldConnection: How we draw when happy versus sad shows in our line quality

lessons.title: Chasse aux formes
lessons.oneGoal: Students identify basic shapes (circle, square, triangle) in their environment

visualSupports: Shape binoculars with cutout viewing holes

then.plan: Hide large paper shapes around classroom beforehand. Students hunt for hidden shapes instead of naturally occurring ones.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Shapes appear in signs, windows, wheels, and everyday objects

lessons.title: Création de lignes libres
lessons.oneGoal: Students practice making various line types with drawing tools

then.plan: Use fingers with different pressures - light touch for thin lines, firm press for thick lines, fingertip dots for pointillé. Draw in sand tray or on textured surfaces.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Different drawing tools create different line qualities for different purposes

lessons.title: Formes avec les mains
lessons.oneGoal: Students create shapes using finger painting and hand printing techniques

visualSupports: Mirror for students to see their hand shapes
Shape examples made with hand prints
Artwork displayed on desks or walls

then.situation: Finger paints unavailable or classroom restrictions
then.plan: Use clay or playdough to create 3D shapes with hands. Students can press hands into clay to make shape impressions.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Hands can create shapes in sand, clay, and other materials

lessons.title: Lignes racontent des histoires
lessons.oneGoal: Students use different lines to illustrate simple stories or experiences

visualSupports: Maps displayed in center of circle

then.situation: Students struggle with personal journey concept
then.plan: Use a familiar story like 'Three Little Pigs' and create the pigs' journey using different lines for different parts of their adventure.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Maps use lines to show paths and journeys we take

lessons.title: Motifs avec des formes
lessons.oneGoal: Students create simple repeating patterns using basic shapes

then.plan: Use cut paper shapes to glue patterns, or create patterns with pattern blocks and copy them by drawing.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Patterns appear in clothing, wallpaper, and nature around us

lessons.title: Lignes et nature
lessons.oneGoal: Students observe and recreate natural line patterns from plants and animals

visualSupports: Natural reference objects available for comparison

then.plan: Use online nature videos or photos on screen. Students can trace line patterns they see in the air, then draw them on paper.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Tree branches, leaf veins, and animal stripes are natural line patterns

lessons.title: Formes géométriques composées
lessons.oneGoal: Students combine basic shapes to create more complex forms and objects

visualSupports: Variety of pre-cut shapes in different sizes

then.plan: Use pattern blocks to build creations and have students draw their constructions. Or use sidewalk chalk outside to draw large shape combinations.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Houses, cars, and toys are made by combining basic shapes

lessons.title: Cultures et motifs
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore line and shape patterns from different cultures

visualSupports: Real cultural objects or high-quality photos

then.plan: Focus on patterns from students' own family backgrounds. Ask students if their families have special decorations or patterns at home.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Every culture decorates objects with special line and shape patterns

lessons.title: Expression personnelle
lessons.oneGoal: Students create original artworks expressing their feelings using lines and shapes

then.plan: Make it less personal - have them create artwork about their favorite animal or color instead, focusing on technique rather than emotion.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Art helps us share our feelings with others through visual language

lessons.title: Critique et appréciation
lessons.oneGoal: Students observe and discuss how lines and shapes work in artworks and daily life

visualSupports: Art prints at student eye level

then.plan: Use student artwork from previous lessons as gallery pieces, or investigate line and shape elements in classroom decorations and displays.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Looking carefully at art and design helps us see beauty everywhere

lessons.title: Portfolio et réflexion
lessons.oneGoal: Students compile their work and reflect on their learning about lines and shapes

visualSupports: Lesson reference cards for teacher prompts
Simple reflection sheets with picture prompts

then.situation: Student artwork is incomplete or missing
then.plan: Focus on memories and learning instead of physical pieces. Students can recreate favorite techniques or demonstrate what they learned through movement and gesture.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Keeping artwork helps us see how our skills grow and change

lessons.title: Lignes dans l'espace
lessons.oneGoal: Students practice creating three-dimensional line sculptures with wire and pipe cleaners

then.plan: Use playdough or clay to create 3D line sculptures by rolling and shaping. Students can make standing line forms that can be viewed from all angles.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Sculptors use lines in space to create artwork we can walk around

lessons.realWorldConnection: Comic books use special lines to show speed and movement

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: ""

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en arts visuels
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
Découverte des lignes, Lignes avec le corps, Lignes émotionnelles, Chasse aux formes, Création de lignes libres

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Valorisez le processus créatif autant que le produit final.

N'hésitez pas à me contacter si vous avez des questions ou si vous souhaitez partager des ressources culturelles liées à cette unité.

La créativité s'épanouit avec votre encouragement!

Cordialement,
[Nom de l'enseignant(e)]
